cards.claim: LLM-based agents overcome the static nature of LLMs by integrating them into multi-step workflows with external tools to enable autonomous planning and interaction.
cards.evidence_quote: LLM-based agents address those gaps by building on LLMs as a backbone, integrating them into multi-step workflows and equipping them with external tools (Wang et al., 2024a).

cards.claim: Evaluating LLM-based agents requires a new paradigm that goes beyond measuring textual outputs to assess sequential decision-making in dynamic environments.
cards.evidence_quote: Such evaluation must go beyond measuring LLM textual outputs to assess an agent’s capacity for sequential decision-making and operation within dynamic environments.

cards.claim: This survey presents the first overview of LLM-based agent evaluation by mapping the current landscape and identifying key gaps for future research.
cards.evidence_quote: In this survey, we present the first overview of LLM-based agent evaluation. We aim to benefit developers, benchmark creators, practitioners, and researchers by mapping the current evaluation landscape and identifying key gaps for future research.

cards.claim: The survey covers fundamental capabilities like planning and tool use, benchmarks for specific agent types, generalist agent leaderboards, core benchmark dimensions, and evaluation frameworks.
cards.evidence_quote: We begin by discussing the evaluation of fundamental LLM-based agent capabilities (§2). These include planning, tool use, self-reflection, and memory. We then review benchmarks and evaluation strategies for prominent types of agentic applications: web agents, software engineering agents, scientific agents, and conversational agents (§3).

cards.claim: Even state-of-the-art models struggle with long-horizon planning tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: Results show that even SOTA models struggle with long-horizon planning.

cards.claim: A standardized benchmark or methodology for assessing self-reflection remains a critical gap in the field.
cards.evidence_quote: Despite these efforts, a standardized benchmark or methodology for assessing self-reflection remains a critical gap.

cards.claim: Function calling is a fundamental ability for agents to deliver updated, contextually accurate responses.
cards.evidence_quote: Function Calling & Tool Use is a fundamental ability for agents to deliver updated, contextually accurate responses (Qin et al., 2023; Tang et al., 2023).

cards.claim: Dedicated benchmarks for agentic memory evaluate episodic memory by assessing how agents leverage prior interactions to support continual improvement across multi-session tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: For episodic memory, Benchmarks evaluate how agents leverage prior interactions and feedback to support continual improvement across multi-session agentic tasks (Wu et al., 2024a; He et al., 2026).

cards.claim: Benchmarks for semantic memory assess retrieval effectiveness and long-range understanding, revealing that current methods remain limited in maintaining long-range consistency.
cards.evidence_quote: For semantic memory, benchmarks assess retrieval effectiveness and long-range understand-ing, revealing that current methods remain limited in maintaining long-range consistency and han-dling dynamic memory (Tan et al., 2025; Hu et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2025).

cards.claim: WebArena provides a dynamic environment with fully functional websites, unlike the offline Mind2Web environment.
cards.evidence_quote: In contrast, WebArena introduces a dynamic environment featuring fully functional websites across multiple domains, enriched with auxiliary tools and knowledge sources.

cards.claim: SWE-bench Verified is the de facto benchmark for assessing software engineering agents due to its high-quality subset of 500 samples.
cards.evidence_quote: The most widely adopted of these, SWE-bench Verified (OpenAI, 2024), carries extensive human filtration and validation to yield a high-quality subset of 500 samples.

cards.claim: Model performance on SWE-bench Pro remains below 25% Pass@1, highlighting limitations in handling complex code changes.
cards.evidence_quote: Model performance remains below 25% Pass@1, highlighting current limitations in handling long-horizon, complex code changes.

cards.claim: WebVoyager exhibits over-optimistic performance estimates compared to the more rigorous Online-Mind2Web.
cards.evidence_quote: However, recent work suggests it exhibits over-optimistic performance estimates, and proposes Online-Mind2Web as a more rigorous alternative that remains challenging for current agents (Xue et al., 2025).

cards.claim: The field is shifting focus toward developing and assessing scientific agents that accelerate research across the full pipeline, including ideation, experiment design, code generation, and peer review.
cards.evidence_quote: Recent advancements have shifted the focus toward developing and assessing scientific agents in accelerating scientific research. New benchmarks span the full research pipeline: (1) Scientific Ideation... (2) Experiment Design... (3) Code Generation... (4) Peer Review...

cards.claim: Conversational agents are designed to perform goal-directed, multi-turn dialogue with users to accomplish specific tasks, extending Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems to real-world interactions.
cards.evidence_quote: Conversational agents are agents designed to perform goal-directed, multi-turn dialogue with a user to accomplish a specific task, such as booking a flight or resolving a customer support issue. This field builds on Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems (TODS), extending it from purely textual tasks to real-world tasks requiring environment interaction.

cards.claim: While τ-Bench assesses agents' ability to interact with simulated users using API tools, it is limited in scale and overlooks policy violations and dialogue flow errors.
cards.evidence_quote: However, it is limited in scale, user simulation setup, and focuses solely on coarse-grained end-to-end metrics, overlooking policy violations and dialogue flow errors.

cards.claim: τ2-Bench addresses previous limitations by introducing a Telecom domain with dynamic environments and a compositional task generator to create diverse, verifiable tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: τ 2-Bench (Barres et al., 2025) addresses these limitations by introducing a Telecom domain, where the user utilizes tools to act in a shared, dynamic environment, and by adding a compositional task generator that programmatically creates diverse, verifiable tasks.

cards.claim: Generalist agent evaluation has evolved into two complementary approaches: benchmarks requiring wide capabilities and unified task-specific benchmarks.
cards.evidence_quote: This shift has led to the development of two complementary approaches to generalist agent evaluation.

cards.claim: The Gaia benchmark requires reasoning, multi-modality, web browsing, and tool-use proficiency on real-world questions.
cards.evidence_quote: Gaia is composed of real-world questions that require abilities such as reasoning, multi-modality handling, web browsing, and tool-use proficiency.

cards.claim: OSWorld evaluates agents via UI interaction, whereas AppWorld and Gaia2 use code and API calls.
cards.evidence_quote: In OSWorld, the agent interacts via UI, while in AppWorld and Gaia2, it uses code and API calls.

cards.claim: Harbor and Exgentic provide frameworks with a unified protocol to solve the lack of cross-benchmark evaluation support.
cards.evidence_quote: Harbor and Exgentic aim to solve that by providing frameworks with a unified protocol for general agent assessment

cards.claim: Most high-quality benchmarks use a hybrid curation strategy combining human validation with automated or synthetic methods rather than relying solely on human annotation.
cards.evidence_quote: High-quality benchmarks rarely rely solely on human-curated data; most employ a hybrid curation strategy.

cards.claim: Static environments fail to capture cascading effects of errors, whereas dynamic environments allow agents to interact with live worlds where actions alter the state.
cards.evidence_quote: Static environments... rely on offline traces or cached web pages... While scalable, these fail to capture the cascading effects of errors

cards.claim: Evaluation metrics vary by task type, using execution-based unit testing for code, state matching for environment modifications, and answer matching for reasoning.
cards.evidence_quote: For SWE tasks... SWE measures are adopted, like execution-based unit testing. Tasks that require modifying the environment state... deploy state matching

cards.claim: Standard benchmarks rarely test safety policies like data privacy, and future benchmarks must integrate guardrail metrics to penalize non-compliant actions.
cards.evidence_quote: Beyond robustness, enterprise agents must adhere to strict policies, such as data privacy and access control, which are rarely tested in standard benchmarks.

cards.claim: General-purpose frameworks for LLM agent evaluation integrate into the development process to enable flexible scenario design and continuous monitoring, unlike static benchmarks.
cards.evidence_quote: Unlike the benchmarks discussed in the preceding sections, which assess fully developed systems using fixed scenarios and standardized test datasets, these frameworks integrate into the development process, enabling flexible, custom scenario design and supporting a broad range of general use cases across both development and deployment.

cards.claim: Final-response evaluation is fast and inexpensive but offers limited insight because it cannot assess intermediate decisions or failure causes within complex workflows.
cards.evidence_quote: Final-response evaluation is fast, inexpensive, and easy to automate, making it well-suited for large-scale monitoring and regression testing. However, it offers limited insight into agent behavior, as it cannot assess intermediate decisions, execution efficiency, or failure causes within complex workflows.

cards.claim: Stepwise evaluation supports granular assessment of individual agent steps to enable error localization and systematic analysis of multi-step execution failures.
cards.evidence_quote: Most frameworks support granular assessments of individual agent steps, such as LLM generations, tool invocations, and routing decisions, enabling error localization and systematic analysis of where and how multi-step executions fail.

cards.claim: Reference-based trajectory methods are limited because multiple valid paths typically exist and manual reference specification is often infeasible.
cards.evidence_quote: However, reference-based methods are inherently limited, as multiple valid paths typically exist and manual reference specification is often infeasible.

cards.claim: Current evaluation frameworks struggle to derive insights across large collections of runs, making it difficult to understand root causes for agent failures at scale.
cards.evidence_quote: deriving insights across large collections of runs remains difficult. Thus, understanding root causes for agent failures at scales is still unsupported.

cards.claim: Current frameworks overlook the cost incurred by the evaluation process itself, specifically when scaling over a large number of traces with expensive LLM judges.
cards.evidence_quote: Second, current frameworks overlook the cost incurred by the evaluation process itself, specifically when scaling over a large number of traces with expensive LLM judges.

cards.claim: Most current frameworks lack built-in support for evaluating safety and policy compliance.
cards.evidence_quote: Finally, most current frameworks lack built-in support for evaluating safety and policy compliance (See §7).

cards.claim: Frameworks provide supporting capabilities for data management and experimentation, including integrated annotation tools and human-in-the-loop evaluation.
cards.evidence_quote: Most offer integrated annotation tools and support human-in-the-loop evaluation, enabling the extraction of evaluation datasets from production logs.

cards.claim: Agent evaluation is shifting from static simulations to dynamic, real-world benchmarks like WebArena and SWE-bench.
cards.evidence_quote: Web agents evolved from basic simulations to dynamic, real-world settings such as WebArena. In software engineering, benchmarks like SWE-bench utilize real GitHub issues, moving beyond synthetic coding tasks.

cards.claim: Static benchmarks become obsolete quickly, necessitating the rise of adaptive live benchmarks like BFCL and SWE-bench Pro.
cards.evidence_quote: Static benchmarks quickly become obsolete, saturated, and abandoned. In response, we see a rise in “live” benchmarks. For instance, the few versions of BFCL, and the refinement of the SWE-bench family (Verified, Pro, and more).

cards.claim: Current evaluations often overlook cost and efficiency, leading to resource-intensive agents that are difficult to deploy.
cards.evidence_quote: Current evaluations often prioritize performance while overlooking cost and efficiency measurements. This emphasis can inadvertently drive the development of highly capable but resource-intensive agents, limiting their practical deployment Kapoor et al. (2024b).

cards.claim: Most benchmarks conflate LLM capabilities with agent harness design, making it hard to attribute performance gains.
cards.evidence_quote: Most current agent benchmarks conflate two distinct evaluation targets: (1) the inherent capabilities of the backbone LLM, and (2) the design of the agent Harness (a.k.a. scaffold).

cards.claim: The survey outlines that LLM-based agent evaluation has progressed from assessing isolated capabilities to evaluating agents in realistic and dynamic environments.
cards.evidence_quote: This survey presents an overview of the evolving field of LLM-based agent evaluation, outlining its progression from assessing isolated capabilities in simplified settings to evaluating agents in realistic, dynamic, and challenging environments.

cards.claim: Future research should focus on developing fine-grained, scalable evaluation methods and establishing standardized metrics for cost-efficiency, safety, and robustness.
cards.evidence_quote: Future research should focus on developing fine-grained, scalable evaluation methods that extend beyond overall success rates, establishing standardized metrics for cost-efficiency, safety, and robustness for responsible deployment.

cards.claim: The survey acknowledges limitations including the dynamic nature of the field, subjective benchmark selection, constrained depth of analysis, and inherent interpretation in future directions.
cards.evidence_quote: While this survey provides a comprehensive overview of the evaluation landscape for LLM-based agents, it is important to acknowledge certain limitations inherent to a review of such a rapidly evolving field.

rejected.claim: LLM-based agents are composed of a backbone LLM and an agent harness, making the evaluation of core LLM abilities essential for understanding their potential.
rejected.evidence_quote: LLM-based agents are composed of a backbone LLM and an agent harness (Yao et al., 2022b). Thus, evaluating the core suite of LLM abilities required for agentic tasks is paramount to understanding the potential and limitations of LLM-based agents.
